Rashi on Shabbat 64a:11:1.hebrew: השתא דאתיא גזירה שוה - וכי היכי דיליף מת משרץ למעוטי חבלים ומשיחות, יליף נמי שרץ ממת לכל מעשה עזים, לרבות קילקלי וחבק:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:11:1.english: Now that the verbal analogy was cited - And just as [the passage of] a corpse derives from [that of] a creeping animal to exclude ropes and cords, so too, [the passage of] a creeping animal derives from [that of] a corpse regarding “all work of goats’ hair,” to include reins and a saddle band.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:12:1.english: I have [this] only with regard to a creeping animal - For "or a sack" is written there.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:14:1.hebrew: אם ריבה - לטמא דבר הבא מזנב הסוס, בטומאת ערב הוא דריבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:14:1.english: If it included - To render impure an item that comes from a horse's tail, it is [only] with regard to impurity [lasting until] evening that it included [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:14:2.hebrew: שהיא מרובה - שכל המגעות טומאת ערב הן — בין דשרץ ונבילה ושכבת זרע, מגע הזב ומגע טמא מת:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:14:2.english: Which is extensive - For all [types of] contact are an impurity [until] evening — whether of a creeping animal, a carcass, or semen, contact with a zav, or contact with one defiled by a corpse.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:14:3.hebrew: נרבה אנו בטומאת ז' שכן מועטת היא - שאינה בכל המגעות, אלא במגע המת בלבד:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:14:3.english: Shall we include [it] in the impurity of seven [days], for it is limited? - For it does not apply to all [forms of] contact, but only to contact with a corpse.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:16:1.hebrew: מופנה - צריך שתהא גזירה שוה זו מב' תיבות, דבגד ועור מופנין למדרש זה, שלא יהו צריכין לגופן. ומאחר שמופנין ללמוד גזירה שוה, ה"ל כמאן דכתיב דרשא בקרא בהדיא, ואין משיבין עליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:16:1.english: Free - It is necessary that this verbal analogy [derive] from two words — that [both] "garment" and "leather" are free for this exposition, so that they are not needed for their own [context]. And since they are free to teach a verbal analogy, it is as though the exposition were written explicitly in the verse, and one does not refute it.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:16:2.hebrew: דאי לאו מופנה - אמרינן: לגופן באו, ולא ילפינן להא מילתא מינייהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:16:2.english: Because if it were not free - We would say: They came for their own [context], and we do not derive this matter from them.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:16:3.hebrew: דאיכא למיפרך כו' - וה"ה דמצי למימר הכי אגזירה שוה קמייתא. ומיהו, אסקי לכולה ברייתא ברישא, ופריך אהא דסליק מינה, ובשינויא דמשנינן בהא מתרצה נמי קמייתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:16:3.english: Because it can be refuted, etc. - And the same applies, that [the Gemara] could have said this regarding the first verbal analogy. However, it concluded the entire baraita first and objected to that with which it concluded; and through the resolution that we give for this one, the first [verbal analogy] is also resolved.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:17:2.english: And it is written regarding it, in [the case of] semen - That garment and leather are impure through it.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:18:1.hebrew: מצד אחד - הכתובין בשרץ מופנים, כדאמרן, אבל הכתובין במת אין מופנין:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:18:1.english: From one side - Those [words] written regarding a creeping animal are free, as we said, but those written regarding a corpse are not free.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:18:2.hebrew: הניחא למ"ד כו' - פלוגתא דרבי ישמעאל ורבנן היא במסכת נדה, בהמפלת (נדה דף כב:):
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:18:2.english: It works out well according to the one who said, etc. - This is a dispute between Rabbi Yishmael and the Rabbis in Tractate Niddah, in [the chapter entitled] Hamappelet (Niddah 22b).

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:18:3.english: Rather, according to the one who said [that] one derives - If there is no refutation.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:18:4.english: And one refutes - If there is [a refutation] to refute [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:18:5.hebrew: מאי איכא למימר - הרי יש להשיב, שכן מטמא בכעדשה:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:18:5.english: What can be said? - Behold, one can refute [it], for [a creeping animal] imparts impurity in [the size of] a lentil.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:19:1.hebrew: והנוגע בכל טמא נפש - או איש אשר תצא ממנו שכבת זרע:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:19:1.english: And whoever touches anything that is impure by the dead - [The verse continues:] “Or a man whose semen is emitted from him.”

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:1:1.hebrew: כלי כלי - בשרצים כתיב: "כל כלי אשר יעשה מלאכה" וגו', ומגופיה דקרא דשרצים לא מצי יליף, ד"אשר יעשה מלאכה" לאו כלי תכשיט משמע:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:1:1.english: “Vessel,” “vessel” - With regard to creeping animals, it is written: “Any vessel with which labor is done…” etc. (Leviticus 11:32), and from the verse regarding creeping animals itself he could not derive [this], as “with which labor is done” does not imply an ornamental vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:20:1.english: A mold of the breasts - In which [the breasts] rest.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:22:1.hebrew: לקלקולכם - של מעשה שטים, לזנות את בנות מואב — שמא כך עשיתם במדין, לכך אתם צריכין קרבן:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:22:1.english: To your corruption - [That] of the incident of Shittim, to commit harlotry with the daughters of Moab: perhaps you did so in Midian, [and] therefore you require an offering.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:22:2.english: Not [one] is missing - [None of us] was lacking the Jewish trait [of modesty].

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:2:1.hebrew: שק - הוא עשוי מנוצה של עזים, שאף על פי שאינו אריג, אלא קלע קטן עשה מנוצה של עזים לתלות בו בתי נפש לצואר בתו — טמא, שדרכו בכך ותכשיט הוא. וה"ק: שהוא טמא משום אריג, ואע"פ שאינו אריג:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:2:1.english: Sack - It is made of goats’ hair, [meaning] that even though it is not woven, but rather he made a small braid of goats’ hair to hang perfume flasks on it around his daughter’s neck, it is ritually impure, for that is its customary use and it is an ornament. And this is what [the baraita] is saying: that it is ritually impure under [the category of] woven fabric, even though it is not woven.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:2:2.hebrew: קולע ג' נימין כו' - ג' חוטין של מטוה של נוצה של עזים צבועה:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:2:2.english: Braids three hairs, etc. - Three threads spun from dyed goat hair.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:2:3.hebrew: ותולה בצואר בתו - וקליעתה זו היא אריגתו, מאחר שהוא טווי, כדאמרן גבי תיכי חלילתא בריש פירקין דקרי להו אריג. והא דקאמר אע"פ שאינו אריג — כלומר, לאו אריג ממש:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:2:3.english: And hangs it on his daughter’s neck - And this braiding of it is its weaving, since it is spun [thread], as we said regarding hollow chains at the beginning of our chapter, where it called them “woven.” And that which [the Gemara] said, “Even though it is not woven” — that is to say, not actual woven [fabric].

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:3:1.english: I have only a sack - That which is made for shepherds' clothing.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:3:2.english: Kilkeli - A horse strap that is called peitral [a breast-collar].

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:3:3.hebrew: חבק - צינגלא של סרגא ואוכף, ועושין אותה מנוצה של עזים, טווי ואריג:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:3:3.english: A saddle band - The girth [cengle] of a saddle and packsaddle; and they make it from goat’s down, spun and woven.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:5:1.hebrew: יכול שאני מרבה החבלים והמשיחות - לציא"ל, שעושין למדוד, וקולעין מן הנוצה כמו שנתלשה, ואינו טווי. ולא דמי לקולע שלש נימין דלעיל, דהתם טווי הוא, וזו היא אריגתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:5:1.english: I might [have thought] that I would include the ropes and the cords - Linoel [cords], which they make for measuring, and they braid [them] from the down [of goats] just as it was plucked, and it is not spun. And it is not similar to one who braids three strands [mentioned] above, for there it is spun, and this [braiding] is its weaving.

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:5:2.english: I might [think] that I would include, etc. - Since 'all' is written [in the verse].

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:5:3.english: And it is a logical deduction that we should not include [them] - And a verse is not needed to exclude [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:6:1.hebrew: הן - תמיה הוא: וכי דברים כוונים הם:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:6:1.english: Indeed - It is an expression of astonishment: Are [these] matters equivalent?

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:6:2.hebrew: אם היקל בטומאת שרץ שהיא קלה - כלומר, אם היקל מלטמא חבלים ומשיחות, היקל לך בשרץ, שטומאתו קלה — טומאת ערב:
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:6:2.english: If [the Torah] was lenient with regard to the impurity of a creeping animal, which is light - That is to say, if it was lenient [by not] rendering ropes and cords impure, it was lenient for you regarding a creeping animal, whose impurity is light — an impurity [lasting until] evening:

Rashi on Shabbat 64a:6:3.hebrew: נקל - גם אנחנו, בבנין אב זה, במת שטומאתו חמורה — טומאת ז':
Rashi on Shabbat 64a:6:3.english: Shall we be lenient - [Shall] we also [be lenient] through this binyan av [general principle] regarding a corpse whose impurity is severe — an impurity of seven [days]?

Tosafot on Shabbat 64a:17:1.hebrew: שמע מינה לאפנויי - הקשה ה"ר אליעזר ממיץ: כיון דאיתקש שרץ ומת לשכבת זרע, א"כ ג"ש דבגד ועור ל"ל? דכל מה שיהיה במת ניתן בשכבת זרע, וכל מה שיהיה בשכבת זרע ניתן בשרץ, וכן להפך — דהא קי"ל: דבר הבא מן ההיקש חוזר ומלמד בהיקש, חוץ מן הקדשים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 64a:17:1.english: "Learn from it [that it is] to render them free" - Rabbi Eliezer of Metz raised a difficulty: Since a creeping animal and a corpse are [both] juxtaposed to semen, if so, why do I need the verbal analogy [gezeirah shavah] of "garment and leather"? For whatever [law] applies to a corpse is transferred to semen, and whatever applies to semen is transferred to a creeping animal, and so too in reverse — for we maintain that a matter derived through a juxtaposition can in turn teach through a juxtaposition, except in [the case of] consecrated items.

Tosafot on Shabbat 64a:22:1.hebrew: מידי הרהור מי יצאנו - וא"ת: והא אפילו יפת תואר הותרה להם? וי"ל: דמכל מקום שייך בה איסור, כדאמרינן (קדושין דף כב.): "וחשקת בה" — ולא בחברתה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 64a:22:1.english: "Did we emerge from the grasps of thoughts [of transgression]?" - And if you say: But wasn't even a beautiful captive woman [yefat to'ar] permitted to them? And one can say: Nevertheless, a prohibition applies to her, as we say (Kiddushin 22a): "[And you desire] her" — and not her companion [meaning, he may not take two captive women].

Tosafot on Shabbat 64a:3:1.hebrew: מניין לרבות את הקילקלי והחבק - ואם תאמר: והא לא מיטלטל מלא וריקן? ואי משום דאפשר לקפלה — אם אינו עשוי לכך, לאו כלום הוא, כדאמר לקמן גבי קב הקיטע, דאע"ג דיש לו בית קיבול לראש שוקו, אם אינו עשוי לקבל — טהור! וי"ל: דהני נמי לשם כל צורכן הן עשוין מתחלה. אך קשה, דלעיל פ' במה מדליקין (שבת דף כז. ושם) מפיק דבר הבא מן העזים דמטמא בשרצים מאו בגד, וקילקלי וחבק באין מן העזים, ומפיק להן הכא מאו שק? וע"ק, דהתם מרבה לנוצה של עזים לג' על ג', ואילו שק שיעורו בד'? ואומר ר"י, דתרי גווני נוצה של עזים הוו: והתם מיירי [בדקה], שעושים ממנה בגדים חשובים, והלכך איתרבו לשלשה על שלשה כמו שאר בגדים; והכא מיירי בנוצה גסה, שממנה עושין קילקלי וחבק וחבלים ומשיחות ושק:
Tosafot on Shabbat 64a:3:1.english:
From where [is it derived] to include the kilkeli and the chavak - And if you say: But isn't [a vessel susceptible to ritual impurity only if it is] moved [both] full and empty? And if [you say that it is susceptible] because it is possible to fold it [into a receptacle] — if it is not made for that [purpose], it is nothing [i.e., of no halakhic effect], as [the Gemara] says later regarding the amputee's wooden leg (66a), that even though it has a receptacle for the stump of his leg, if it is not made to hold [objects], it is pure! And one can say: These, too, are made from the outset for whatever need they may serve.
However, it is difficult: for above, in the chapter [entitled] "Bameh Madlikin" (Shabbat 27a, and there [in Tosafot]), [the Gemara] derives that an item that comes from goats becomes impure through [contact with] crawling creatures from "or cloth," and kilkeli and chavak come from goats, yet here it derives them from "or sack"! And furthermore, it is difficult: for there, [the Gemara] includes goat's down for [a minimum size of] three by three [fingerbreadths], whereas sackcloth, its measure is four [by four handbreadths]! And Ri says: There are two kinds of goat's down. And there [on 27a], it deals with fine [down], from which they make high-quality garments, and therefore they were included for [a minimum size of] three by three [fingerbreadths], like other garments; but here [on 64a], it deals with coarse hair, from which they make kilkeli, chavak, ropes, cords, and sackcloth.
